speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I will be evaluating the skin condition on your left dorsal hand; please describe the appearance, size, and any symptoms like itching, pain, or fluid leakage associated with the lesion. To assist me, may I also see a clear photograph of the affected area?

speaker: Patient
text: 65-year-old female. The patient is here for an annual well-check. She has a history of well-controlled diabetes and hypertension, managed with metformin and losartan, respectively. She reports maintaining a healthy diet primarily consisting of vegetables and lean meat, denies any tobacco or alcohol use, and enjoys outdoor activities like walking and sunbathing.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history, Mrs. 65. Given your sunbathing habits and the location of the lesion on your left dorsal hand, could you describe the specific appearance of the spot, its exact dimensions, and whether it has been changing over time? Please also let me know if it has any central clearing or scaly borders.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is The presence of a rough, scaly, sandpaper-like plaque on the left dorsal hand. I also have No tenderness, No pain.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Actinic Keratosis. The description of a rough, scaly, sandpaper-like plaque on the dorsum of the hand in a sun-exposed individual with a history of sunbathing is classic for this premalignant condition. Given your age and risk factors, I recommend a skin biopsy to confirm the diagnosis and rule out squamous cell carcinoma.
